title: Chapter 2.2 — Solving Inequalities Using Addition or Subtraction

cards.back: Inequalities that have the same solution set. They are produced by applying properties of inequality.
Adding the same number to each side of an inequality produces an equivalent inequality. If $ a > b $, then $ a + c > b + c $. Applies to all symbols.
Add 6 to both sides: $ x \ge -4 $. Graph: closed circle at -4, shade right.
Subtracting the same number from each side of an inequality produces an equivalent inequality. If $ a > b $, then $ a - c > b - c $.
Subtract 8 from both sides: $ y \le -3 $. Graph: closed circle at -3, shade left.
Subtract 1.4: $ -9.4 < m $. Rewrite: $ m > -9.4 $. Graph: open circle at -9.4, shade right.

cards.front: When solving $ k + 5 \le -3 $, what operation should you use?
cards.back: Subtract 5 from both sides (Subtraction Property of Inequality) to isolate $ k $.

cards.front: How do you check a solution of an inequality?
cards.back: [[imp:Substitute]] a value from the solution set into the original inequality. If the statement is true, it's correct. Test a few values around the boundary.

cards.front: Why do you simplify each side before solving an inequality?
cards.back: Combining like terms first makes the inequality [[imp:cleaner and easier to solve]], reducing potential errors.
Simplify left: $ j + 6 < 8 $. Subtract 6: $ j < 2 $. Graph: open circle at 2, shade left.
Combine like terms on right: $ 10 \ge p - 7 $. Add 7: $ 17 \ge p $, or $ p \le 17 $. Graph: closed circle at 17, shade left.

cards.front: A microwave uses 1100 W on a 1800 W circuit. Write and solve an inequality for additional watts $ w $.
cards.back: $ 1100 + w < 1800 $. Subtract 1100: $ w < 700 $. You can add less than 700 watts.

cards.front: A carry‑on bag weighs 38 lb, max 50 lb. Write and solve for extra weight $ x $.
cards.back: $ 38 + x \le 50 $. Subtract 38: $ x \le 12 $. You can add up to 12 pounds.
Flip the symbol: $ m > -9.4 $. The small end still points to the smaller number.
cards.front: How does the inequality symbol change when you rewrite $ -9.4 < m $ with $ m $ on the left?
What is the blueprint for solving inequalities with addition/subtraction?
cards.back: [[imp:Understand]] (identify variable, operation, symbol) → [[imp:Solve]] (add/subtract to isolate, simplify first) → [[imp:Conclude]] (graph and interpret).
